newsitem.title: ITALY: Breakdown of troops in Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Breakdown of troops in Albania force.

text.p: The Italian-led security force being assembled for deployment in Albania is expected to number up to 6,000 men from at least eight nations.

Defence sources say it is likely to be led on the ground by General Luciano Forlani, the 57-year-old commander of Italy's Third Armoured Corps and a former commander of the Italian division assigned to NATO's rapid intervention forces.
Following are details of nations and numbers:
-- Italy is expected to provide 2,000 to 2,500 troops, including mechanised infantry, paratroopers, light armoured forces, army and navy commando units and air support.
-- France, 1,000 troops made up of mechanised marine units plus helicopters, armoured personnel carriers and other armoured fighting vehicles.
Austria says it will contribute an unspecified number of soldiers and police. Denmark is also taking part, according to Italian officials.
The force will be deployed at Tirana airport and the Adriatic ports of Durres, Vlore and possibly Sarande to protect relief convoys around the country.
